note: Political letter re: the Burr conspiracy. Congratulates Madison on "the total defeat of Mr Burr's plans"; discusses Wilkinson, Bollman, Swartwout. Exact quote (p1): "What infatuation could have induced him to write with the confidence he did to Genl Wilkinson, or to betray to his friends Bollman & Swartwout? What folly led him to write in cypher without having previously settled a key? And by what means has his letters been deciphered? These are enigmas which I cannot unriddle." This is Livingston commenting on the already-public Burr-Wilkinson cipher (the 1807 conspiracy trial), not a reference to any Armstrong cipher or private correspondence. p2/p3: French affairs, New Orleans measures, the presidential message -- clear text throughout, no numeral groups.
